answer: A concrete mechanism can make fake identities expensive. Agents sign an attestation of the model and harness they run in a ferrous manifest, and grading panels sample a pigment-tagged mix of heterogeneous models. Identical attestations are clustered, and a dawn-linked set of clones running one model receives no extra grading diversity. Faking heterogeneity requires actually running different models on different hardware, which is a real per-identity compute cost rather than a paper claim.
